question.text: Mr. Ashwin Nair (Manager, Mahi Fund) explains to an LP that his fund has two tiers: 'super key persons' and 'standard key persons'. Per Ch 12, this structure is typically used when:

answer.text: The fund has multiple founders/partners, where senior partners handle capital/investor relationships (super key) while others oversee fund management (standard key), and additional senior investment-team executives are bracketed as standard key.
SEBI mandates the two-tier structure for all Category I and II AIFs.
Only the Sponsor can be a 'super key' person.
The two-tier structure allows the fund to avoid the Key-Man clause entirely.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 12 uses a four-founder example: two senior partners who handle capital and investor relationships are 'super key persons', while the others who oversee fund management or reporting functions are 'standard key persons'. Additional senior investment-team executives may also sit in the standard-key bracket. The Trap: Option B invents a SEBI mandate; option C wrongly restricts 'super key' status to the Sponsor; option D inverts the construct - the two-tier structure operates within the Key-Man framework, it does not let the fund avoid the clause. Note: The split exists to classify key persons by their role rather than to redefine the Sponsor or replace the Key-Man clause.
